etymology: Webster 1828 defines THUS as an adverb: in this or that manner; on this wise. His own biblical illustrations are thus saith the Lord, the Pharisee who prayed thus, and Genesis 6:22 (THUS did Noah, according to all that God commanded him). This page fills the KJV-gap adverb of manner. Companion pages already treat saith, command, and tradition.
biblical_def: Thus in Scripture is not a vibe and not a shrug. It names the manner God has spoken, the manner the saint must walk, and the manner the rebel has emptied the commandment. The prophets do not invent a voice: Thus saith the Lord GOD, It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass (Isa 7:7). Noah does not improvise an ark: Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he (Gen 6:22). Jesus will not let John treat baptism as optional theater: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness (Matt 3:15). The cross is not an accident: how then shall the scriptures be fulfilled, that thus it must be? (Matt 26:54). The clay is not licensed to lecture the Potter: Why hast thou made me thus? (Rom 9:20). The dictionary therefore keeps thus from becoming a private inner oracle. It is the Bible’s way of saying: in this manner, as the Lord has spoken, and no other.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines THUS as in this or that manner; on this wise (thus saith the Lord; the Pharisee prayed thus); then to this degree or extent; and in the phrase thus much, as this much.
webster_full: THUS, adverb In this or that manner; on this wise; as, thus saith the Lord; the Pharisee prayed thus.
THUS did Noah, according to all that God commanded him. Genesis 6:22.
1. To this degree or extent; as thus wise; thus peaceable.
THUS far extend, thus far thy bounds--
2. In the phrase, thus much, it seems to be an adjective, equivalent to this much.
scriptures: Genesis 6:22
Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.
Isaiah 7:7
Thus saith the Lord GOD, It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass.
Matthew 3:15
And Jesus answering said unto him, Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness. Then he suffered him.
Matthew 26:54
But how then shall the scriptures be fulfilled, that thus it must be?
Romans 9:20
Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?
corruption_summary: Thus is corrupted when a private inner voice steals thus saith the Lord, when tradition is allowed to make the commandment of none effect, and when the clay lectures the Potter about how it ought to have been made.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is to mint a new thus saith. Isaiah 7:7 is the Lord GOD speaking; it is not a journaling prompt. Continuationist apostle-and-prophet claims (NAR, Bethel, IHOP) treat impression as oracle. The closed canon is the rule. The recovery is: if the Lord has not spoken it in Scripture, do not stamp it thus.

The second corruption is tradition emptying the commandment. Matthew 15:6 uses the English Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition. Attractional religion and therapeutic religion keep the same move: the Word is adjusted until it no longer binds. Jesus names the manner: you have done it thus.

The third corruption is the clay’s lawsuit. Romans 9:20 will not let the thing formed ask, Why hast thou made me thus? Open theism and process theology deny the Potter His right. The adverb remains the Potter’s. Election is not a manner the creature gets to redesign.
roots_summary: Webster: in this or that manner; on this wise. Genesis 6:22 carries no Strong’s tag on Thus in this cache; this page does not mint one. Companion pages treat saith, command, and tradition.

Greek houtos (G3779) — in this way, thus (Matt 3:15; Matt 26:54; Rom 9:20).
Genesis 6:22 is KJV-verified; the cache does not tag Thus with a Hebrew number on that verse line. No lemma is invented here.
Matthew 15:6 English Thus sits on G2532 (kai) in this cache; that connective is not treated as a minted thus-lemma on this page.
usage: Thus saith the Lord GOD (Isa 7:7) — the manner is the Lord’s speech, not a private impression.
Noah built thus: according to all that God commanded him (Gen 6:22).
The cross must be thus because the Scriptures said so (Matt 26:54); the clay does not get to ask why it was made thus (Rom 9:20).

etymology: Webster 1828 treats YET first as a conjunction: nevertheless; notwithstanding; however. He then lists the adverbial uses: beside; still; at this time / so soon (Not yet); at least; a little longer; still, in a new degree; even, after all; hitherto. His own biblical illustration is Matthew 6:29 (YET I say unto you…). This page fills the KJV-gap particle. Companion pages already treat nevertheless, sinner, and hope.
biblical_def: Yet in Scripture is not a stall and not a loophole. It names what has not come, what remains true against appearance, and what was true of us when Christ died. Jesus will not let His mother hurry the hour: mine hour is not yet come (John 2:4). Paul will not let the cross wait for our improvement: while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us (Rom 5:8). He will not let the servant of Christ keep a second master: if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ (Gal 1:10). Habakkuk will not let empty barns cancel worship: Yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will joy in the God of my salvation (Hab 3:18). John will not let present sonship pretend to be finished glory: it doth not yet appear what we shall be (1 John 3:2). The dictionary therefore keeps yet from becoming either delay-of-obedience or denial-of-hope. It is the Bible’s way of saying: still, nevertheless, and not yet — on God’s clock, not ours.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines YET as a conjunction (nevertheless; notwithstanding; however) and as an adverb: beside; still; at this time / not yet; at least; a little longer; still in a new degree; even after all; hitherto.
webster_full: YET, conjunction [Gr.] Nevertheless; notwithstanding; however. I come to you in the spirit of peace; yet you will not receive me.
YET I say unto you, the Solomon in all his glory, was not arrayed like one of these. Matthew 6:29.
YET, adverb
1. Beside; over and above. There is one reason yet further to be alledged.
2. Still; the state remaining the same.
They attest facts they had heard while they were yet heathens.
3. At this time; so soon. Is it time to go? Not yet.
4. At least; at all.
5. It is prefixed to words denoting extension of time or continuance. A little longer; yet a little longer.
6. Still; in a new degree. The crime becomes yet blacker by the pretense of piety.
7. Even; after all; a kind of emphatical addition to a negative.
8. Hitherto. You have yet done nothing; you have as yet done less than was expected.
scriptures: John 2:4
Jesus saith unto her, Woman, what have I to do with thee? mine hour is not yet come.
Romans 5:8
But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
Galatians 1:10
For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.
Habakkuk 3:18
Yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will joy in the God of my salvation.
1 John 3:2
Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.
corruption_summary: Yet is corrupted when not yet is used to postpone obedience, when yet sinners is used to postpone repentance, and when men-pleasing is kept as a second service beside Christ.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is to steal John 2:4. Mine hour is not yet come is the Son’s clock, not a license to delay what He has already commanded. Soft religion treats every hard duty as not yet. The recovery is: where Scripture has spoken, the hour has come.

The second corruption is cheap grace wearing Romans 5:8. While we were yet sinners, Christ died for us is particular love at the cross, not permission to remain in the sin. Antinomian talk hears yet as forever. Paul hears it as the time of our death in Adam, already met by Christ’s death for the elect.

The third corruption is Galatians 1:10 with a smile. If I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ is not a branding problem. Attractional ministry and people-pleasing pulpits keep a second yet. The servant of Christ cannot keep it.
roots_summary: Webster: nevertheless / still / not yet. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek oupo (G3768) at John 2:4 and 1 John 3:2 (not yet); Greek eti (G2089) at Romans 5:8 and Galatians 1:10. Habakkuk 3:18 carries no Strong’s tag on Yet in this cache; this page does not mint a Hebrew number for that line.
roots_lines: Greek eti (G2089) — yet, still, even now (Rom 5:8, yet sinners; Gal 1:10, if I yet pleased men).
Habakkuk 3:18 is KJV-verified; the cache does not tag Yet with a Hebrew number on that verse line. No lemma is invented here.
Matthew 6:29 English And yet sits on G1161 (de) in this cache; that connective is not treated as a minted yet-lemma on this page.
usage: Mine hour is not yet come (John 2:4) — the Son’s clock, not a delay of commanded duty.
Christ died for us while we were yet sinners (Rom 5:8); that yet is the time of our ruin, not a forever permit.
Habakkuk will yet rejoice when the fields fail (Hab 3:18); Paul will not yet please men and still be Christ’s servant (Gal 1:10).

etymology: Webster 1828 treats LIKE as adjective (equal; similar / resembling; probable), noun (an equal; a resembling person or thing), adverb (in the same manner; in a manner becoming), and verb (to be pleased with in a moderate degree; to approve — less than love). His own biblical illustrations include James 5:17 (Elias was a man subject to like passions as we are), Revelation 18:18, Daniel 1:19, Matthew 6 / Luke 12 (Solomon not arrayed like one of these), Psalm 103, and 1 Samuel 4:9. This page fills the KJV-gap word of resemblance. Companion pages already treat image, similitude, and idolatry.
biblical_def: Like in Scripture is not a brand preference and not a therapy mirror. It names resemblance that either honors God or steals His glory. Jesus will not let prayer copy the heathen: Be not ye therefore like unto them (Matt 6:8). Paul will not let worship shrink God to a mammal: changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man (Rom 1:23). The Son took real flesh: it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren (Heb 2:17). Elijah was not a marble saint: Elias was a man subject to like passions as we are (Jas 5:17). John will not let present sonship pretend to be finished glory, and he will not let glory be anything less than Christ: when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is (1 John 3:2). The dictionary therefore keeps like from becoming either idolatry or self-esteem. It is the Bible’s way of saying: resembling this, and not that.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines LIKE as equal or similar; a resembling person or thing; in the same manner; and as a verb, to be pleased with in a moderate degree (less than love). He illustrates from James 5:17, Revelation, Daniel, Matthew 6, Psalm 103, and 1 Samuel 4:9.
webster_full: LIKE, adjective [Latin , Heb., Gr. See Lick and Lickerish.]
1. Equal in quantity, quality or degree; as a territory of like extent with another; men of like excellence.
2. Similar; resembling; having resemblance.
Elias was a man subject to like passions as we are. James 5:17.
LIKE is usually followed by to or unto, but it is often omitted.
What city is like unto this great city? Revelation 18:18.
I saw three unclean spirits like frogs. Revelation 16:13.
Among them all was found none like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. Daniel 1:19.
3. Probably; likely, that is, having the resemblance or appearance of an event; giving reason to expect or believe.
He is like to die of hunger in the place where he is, for there is no more bread. Jeremiah 38:9.
LIKE, noun [elliptically, for like thing, like event, like person.]
1. Some person or thing resembling another; an equal.
LIKE, adverb
1. In the same manner.
Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. Matthew 6:29. Luke 12:27.
LIKE as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him. Psalms 103.
2. In a manner becoming.
Be strong, and quit yourselves like men. 1 Samuel 4:9.
LIKE, verb transitive
1. To be pleased with in a moderate degree; to approve. It expresses less than love and delight.
scriptures: Matthew 6:8
Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.
Romans 1:23
And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.
Hebrews 2:17

Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.
James 5:17
Elias was a man subject to like passions as we are, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain: and it rained not on the earth by the space of three years and six months.
1 John 3:2
Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.
corruption_summary: Like is corrupted when prayer copies the heathen, when God is recast in man’s image, and when we shall be like him is swapped for a mirror that only likes the self.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is Matthew 6:8 inverted. Be not ye therefore like unto them forbids pagan prayer-copying. Attractional worship copies the street and calls it relevance. The Father already knows. Likeness to the heathen is not mission; it is disobedience.

The second corruption is Romans 1:23. Glory is changed into an image made like to corruptible man. Process theology and every homemade god shrink the uncorruptible God until He resembles the worshiper. That is idolatry. The recovery is: God is not like us; we are to be made like the Son.

The third corruption is to steal 1 John 3:2. We shall be like him is glorification at His appearing, not a present self-esteem slogan. Therapeutic religion wants a God who is like me now. John points to the appearing. Hebrews 2:17 already told the other half: the Son was made like His brethren in true flesh, not in our sin.
roots_summary: Webster: similar / in the same manner / to be pleased with. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek homoioo (G3666) at Matthew 6:8 and Hebrews 2:17; Greek homoioma (G3667) at Romans 1:23; Greek homoios (G3664) at 1 John 3:2; Greek homoiopathes (G3663) at James 5:17 (tagged on the like passions phrase, not as a separate English like token). No Hebrew number is minted on this page.
roots_lines: Greek homoioo (G3666) — to make like, to be like (Matt 6:8; Heb 2:17).
Greek homoioma (G3667) — likeness, image (Rom 1:23, made like to corruptible man).
Greek homoios (G3664) — like, resembling (1 John 3:2, we shall be like him).
Greek homoiopathes (G3663) — of like passions (Jas 5:17). The cache tags the phrase, not a free-standing English like. This page does not invent a second number.
usage: Be not ye therefore like unto them (Matt 6:8) — prayer is not copied from the heathen.
Idolatry makes God like corruptible man (Rom 1:23); the gospel makes the Son like unto his brethren in true flesh (Heb 2:17).
Elijah had like passions (Jas 5:17); the saints will be like him when He appears (1 John 3:2).
